Read a .asc chromatogram from an old AKTA Pure

Source: R/read_akta_old.R
read_akta_old.Rd

Each trace in an ÄKTA export is recorded at its own volumes. The traces are combined into one row per volume of the UV trace, and the other traces are interpolated onto those volumes. The fraction marks give the fraction of each row; rows before the first mark, or after a mark such as "Waste", have no fraction. Injection marks and the logbook are dropped.

Usage

read_akta_old(file, fraction_size = deprecated())

Arguments

file

Filepath to read

fraction_size

Not used: the end of each fraction is given by the next mark.

Value

A chromatogram: a tibble with the run's metadata, see chrom_meta().

Columns

The readers all give one row per sampled point, with the columns the instrument recorded:

  • time, in seconds, when the instrument records it, and volume, in mL.

  • fraction, the fraction each row was collected into, or NA when it wasn't collected.

  • Absorbance, named after its wavelength in nm, such as a280, or uv when the instrument doesn't record the wavelength.

  • The other traces under standard names: conductivity, conductivity_percent, percent_b, pressure, flow and temperature.

fraction is a fraction vector and the absorbance columns are absorbance vectors, which record their wavelength and unit. The other columns are quantity vectors with the unit recorded in the file, such as s, mL, mS/cm, psi or MPa.

Examples

fl <- system.file('extdata', 'example_akta_2.asc', package = 'chromr')

read_akta_old(fl)
#> # A chromatogram: 962 × 9
#> # Instrument:     ÄKTA
#> # Run:            Emma K 15032024 SFPQ FL 2x 800 mL cultures 9 mL loop001:10
#>    volume fraction    uv conductivity conductivity_percent percent_b pressure
